Rashi on Yevamot 14b:10:1.hebrew: מן הספק - קא ס"ד השתא באיסור ספק, כגון מגרש ולנה עמו בפונדקי, דליכא אלא ספק דשמא בא עליה לשם קידושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:10:1.english: From the uncertain [cases] - It enters our mind now [that this refers to] an uncertain prohibition, such as one who divorced [his wife] and she lodged with him in an inn, where there is only a doubt that perhaps he had relations with her for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:12:1.hebrew: לצרה עצמה - הא דקתני נמנעים, מצרה עצמה; ולעולם ב"ש נמי נמנעים מב"ה, מלישא צרת הבת בלא חליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:12:1.english: For the rival wife herself - That which is taught, "They refrained," [means] from the rival wife herself; and indeed, Beit Shammai also refrained from [marrying into] Beit Hillel, [namely,] from marrying the rival wife of a daughter without chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:3:1.hebrew: ומאי אולמיה דהאי מהאי - דקאמר ה"נ מסתברא דמודעי להו, מהאי היכי מסתברא טפי:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:3:1.english: And in what way is this [case] stronger than that [case] - In that it said, "So too it is reasonable that they would inform them" — from this [case], how is it more reasonable?

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:3:2.hebrew: קלא אית לה - ולא צריך לאודועי, ומהתם לא תילף דמודעי:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:3:2.english: [The matter] has publicity - And there is no need to inform [them], and from there you would not derive that they inform [them].

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג: פשיטא, בני חייבי לאוין כשרים נינהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:4:1.english: This is the reading: "It is obvious: the children of those liable to negative commandments are fit."

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:6:1.english: [That] of Rabbi Akiva - [This is taught] below in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 49a).

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:7:1.english: With regard to rival wives - In our Mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:7:2.english: And with regard to sisters - In the chapter 'Four Brothers' (below, Yevamot 26a).

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:8:1.hebrew: ובספק אשת איש - בפרק ב"ש (לקמן יבמות קז.), דתנן: בש"א, "אין ממאנים אלא ארוסות", וכו'. והקטנה בת מיאון קרי "ספק אשת איש", דלמא ממאנת ונפקא. לישנא אחרינא נראה: שכיב מרע שכתב לאשה, "זה גיטיך מהיום אם מתי מחולי זה" — כל אותם הימים נקראת "ספק אשת איש", כדתנן (גיטין דף עד.): "מה היא כל אותן הימים? ר' יוסי אומר: בעילתו ספק; ר"מ אומר: בעילתו תלויה". ותנן: "לא תתייחד עמו אלא ע"פ עדים". אע"פ שלא שנינו בה מחלוקת ב"ש וב"ה, על כרחך נחלקו בה אותו מחלוקת שנחלקו במגרש את אשתו ולנה עמו בפונדק (שם דף פא.): לב"ש, דאמרי לא אמרי' "הן הן עדי ייחוד הן הן עדי ביאה" — אינה צריכה הימנו גט שני; ולב"ה, דאמרי "הן הן עידי ייחוד הן הן עדי ביאה" — צריכה הימנו גט שני. ובפ' מי שאחזו קורדייקוס (שם עג:) איפליגו בה ר' יוסי בר' יהודה ורבנן, דקתני: "ראוה שנתייחדה עמו באפלה כו'". ומוקמינן התם דאליבא דב"ה דמגרש אשתו ולנה עמו בפונדקי הוא דאיפליגו בה, דאמר: כמאן אזלא הא דא"ר יוחנן, "מחלוקת כשראוה כשנבעלה כו'"? וההיא דר' יוחנן, גבי פלוגתא דב"ש וב"ה איתמר:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:8:1.english: And with regard to an uncertain married woman - In the chapter [beginning] 'Beit Shammai' (below, Yevamot 107a), as we learned in a mishna: Beit Shammai say: [Minors] may perform refusal only [when they are] betrothed, etc. And [the baraita here] calls a minor who is eligible for refusal 'an uncertain married woman,' as perhaps she will perform refusal and leave [free of marriage]. According to another version, it appears [to refer to]: A person on his deathbed [shekhiv mera] who wrote to [his] wife, 'This is your bill of divorce from today if I die from this illness' — throughout all those days she is called 'an uncertain married woman,' as we learned in a mishna (Gittin 74a): 'What is her status throughout all those days? Rabbi Yosei says: Intercourse with him is of uncertain status; Rabbi Meir says: Intercourse with him is suspended.' And we learned [in a mishna, Gittin 73a]: 'She may not be secluded with him except in the presence of witnesses.' Even though we did not learn [explicitly in that mishna] a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, perforce they disagreed in this case [with] the very same dispute that they disagreed on regarding one who divorces his wife and she lodged with him at an inn (ibid. 81a): According to Beit Shammai, who say that we do not say 'the very witnesses to seclusion are the witnesses to intercourse,' she does not require a second bill of divorce from him; whereas according to Beit Hillel, who say 'the very witnesses to seclusion are the witnesses to intercourse,' she does require a second bill of divorce from him. And in the chapter [beginning] 'Mi SheAchazo Kurdayakos' (ibid. 73b), Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis disagreed regarding it, as it is taught: 'If they saw that she was secluded with him in the dark, etc.' And we establish there that it is in accordance with [the opinion of] Beit Hillel regarding one who divorces his wife and she lodged with him at an inn that they disagreed regarding it, for [the Gemara there] says: 'In accordance with whom does that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said go: The dispute is when they saw that she engaged in intercourse, etc.?' And that [statement] of Rabbi Yoḥanan was stated regarding the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:8:2.english: An outdated bill of divorce - [And] one who divorces his wife and she lodged with him at an inn [are taught] in Tractate Gittin, in [the chapter] HaZorek (81a).

Rashi on Yevamot 14b:9:1.hebrew: בכסף ושוה כסף בפרוטה ושוה פרוטה - לענין קידושי אשה: ב"ש אומרים בדינר ושוה דינר, ובה"א בפרוטה ושוה פרוטה. ודינר הוא כסף צורי, ופרוטה היא של נחושת. וה"ק הכא: בכסף ובשוה כסף — לב"ש, בפרוטה ובשוה פרוטה — לב"ה. ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף יא.) קרי לדינר דב"ש כסף, דאמר רב אסי: כל כסף האמור בתורה סתם — כסף צורי, ואותבינן: והרי קידושי אשה כו', לימא רב אסי דאמר כב"ש:
Rashi on Yevamot 14b:9:1.english: By money and the equivalent of money, by a peruta and the equivalent of a peruta - With regard to the betrothal of a woman: Beit Shammai say [it is effected] with a dinar and the equivalent of a dinar, and Beit Hillel say [it is effected] with a peruta and the equivalent of a peruta. And a dinar is Tyrian silver, and a peruta is of copper. And this is what [the Gemara] is saying here: 'By money and the equivalent of money' is according to Beit Shammai; 'by a peruta and the equivalent of a peruta' is according to Beit Hillel. And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (11a), [the Gemara] calls Beit Shammai's dinar 'money,' for Rav Asi said: 'Any money mentioned in the Torah without specification is Tyrian silver,' and we objected: 'Behold, the betrothal of a woman, etc., shall we say that Rav Asi spoke in accordance with Beit Shammai?'

Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:12:1.hebrew: אלא ב"ש אמאי נמנעים מב"ה - וא"ת: ודלמא משום ממאנת ומשום ההיא דשוה כסף ככסף היו נמנעים — דאם נתקדשה לראשון בפרוטה ולשני בדינר, לב"ש מקודשת לשני, ובניה מן הראשון ממזרים? ואומר ר"י, דעיקר הך ברייתא משום צרות קתני לה [ולכך קתני לה גבי מתני' דהכא], דלגבי הכי קתני לה מתני', ומשמע משום צרות גרידא היו נמנעים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:12:1.english: "However, why did Beit Shammai refrain from Beit Hillel?" - And if you say: But perhaps they refrained on account of a woman who performed refusal [me'anent], and on account of that [dispute regarding] the equivalent of money like money — for if she was betrothed to a first [man] with a peruta and to a second [man] with a dinar, according to Beit Shammai she is betrothed to the second, and her children from the first are mamzerim? And the Ri says that the primary focus of this baraita was taught on account of rival wives [and for this reason it was taught in connection with the Mishnah here], for in relation to this the Mishnah taught it, and it implies that on account of rival wives alone they would refrain.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:1:1.hebrew: בשלמא ב"ש לא נמנעו מב"ה כו' - להאי גירסא, לא מוכח מהכא אלא דלמ"ד "עשו" אודועי מודעי להו. אבל ר"ח גריס איפכא: "בשלמא ב"ה לא נמנעו מב"ש, דטומאות דב"ש לב"ה טהורות נינהו". וזאת הגירסא נראית, דבכל מקום ב"ש מחמיר לענין טומאה; דכי חשיב בעדיות (פ"ה) קולי דב"ש וחומרי דב"ה, לא חשיב אלא תרי מילי דטומאה וטהרה, אבל כל שאר מילי דטומאה וטהרה — כגון שדרה וגולגולת ושוקת יהוא — הוו ב"ש לחומרא. והשתא, לפי האי גירסא מוכח שפיר דאודועי מודעי להו [אפי' לא עשו] — דליכא למימר דלא נמנעו ב"ש מב"ה משום דלא עשו ב"ש כדבריהם והיו עושין בכל דבר כב"ה ואפי' לקולא, כדמוכח לקמן; דהא טעמא דלא עשו משום אגודות, ובטומאה ובטהרה דב"ש לחומר' היה להם לב"ש למנוע מלעשו' טהרות אגב כלים דב"ה, דליכא אגודות, דהרואה אומר "לא צריכי לכלים דידהו", כדאמר גבי שוקת בית יהוא: "הרואה אומר לאפושי מיא הוא דעבדי"; אלא ודאי ע"כ אודועי הוו מודעי להו, אפילו למ"ד לא עשו. והא דקאמר: "בשלמא בית הלל לא נמנעו מב"ש, דטומאות דב"ש לב"ה טהורות נינהו" — ואע"ג דבתרי מילי ב"ש לקולא, הני תרי מילי לא שכיחי; א"נ, נקט "בשלמא" משום אליבא דמ"ד לא עשו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:1:1.english: "Granted, Beit Shammai did not refrain from Beit Hillel, etc." - According to this reading, it is proven from here only that according to the one who says [they] acted [in practice], they would notify them. However, Rabbeinu Chananel reads the opposite: "Granted, Beit Hillel did not refrain from Beit Shammai, as the impurities of Beit Shammai are pure for Beit Hillel." And this reading appears [correct], for everywhere Beit Shammai is stringent regarding ritual impurity; for when [the Mishnah] in Eduyot (ch. 5) counts the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel, it counts only two matters of ritual impurity and purity, whereas in all other matters of ritual impurity and purity — such as a spine and a skull, and the trough of Yehu — Beit Shammai were stringent. And now, according to this reading, it is well proven that they would notify them, [even according to the one who says] "they did not act" [in practice] — for one cannot say that Beit Shammai did not refrain from Beit Hillel because Beit Shammai did not act in accordance with their own views and would conduct themselves in everything in accordance with Beit Hillel, even leniently, as is proven below; for the reason that they did not act was because of [the prohibition against forming separate] factions, and in [matters of] ritual impurity and purity where Beit Shammai are stringent, Beit Shammai should have refrained from preparing pure foods using the vessels of Beit Hillel, since there is no [concern of] factions, as an onlooker would say, "They do not need their vessels," just as [the Gemara] says concerning the trough of the House of Yehu: "An onlooker says: It is to increase the water that they are doing [this]"; rather, certainly, perforce, they would notify them, even according to the one who says "they did not act." And as for that which [the Gemara] says: "Granted, Beit Hillel did not refrain from Beit Shammai, as the impurities of Beit Shammai are pure for Beit Hillel" — even though in two matters Beit Shammai are lenient [and Beit Hillel are stringent], those two matters are not common; alternatively, it formulated [the argument with] "Granted" (bishlama) because [it is] in accordance with the one who says "they did not act".

Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:4:1.hebrew: פשיטא בני חייבי לאוין כשרים נינהו - תימה, דלא מסיק אדעתי' דאתא לאפוקי מדר"ע. ואי הוה האי ר' אלעזר אמורא — הוה א"ש, דפשיטא ליה דאין הלכה כר"ע; אבל הוא רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, שהוא תנא, כדמוכח בעשרה יוחסין (קדושין עה:). ונראה, דס"ד דלשום תנא לא הוי ממזר מיבמה לשוק, אלא דוקא מחייבי לאוין דשאר, כדתנן בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות מט. ושם): "איזהו ממזר? כל שאר בשר שהוא בלא יבא". והא דתנן בהאשה רבה (לקמן יבמות ד' צב. ושם): "האשה שהלך בעלה ובנה למד"ה, ואמרו מת בעלה ואח"כ מת בנה, ונשאת, ואח"כ אמרו לה חילוף היו הדברים — תצא (מזה ומזה), והולד ממזר (מזה ומזה)", משמע דהוי ממזר מיבמה לשוק — קס"ד דקנסא בעלמא הוא; אע"ג דתניא בגמ': "זו דברי ר"ע, דאמר אין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין" — ההיא ברייתא לא שמיע ליה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:4:1.english: "[This is] obvious; the offspring of those liable for negative prohibitions are fit" - [It is] puzzling that it did not enter [the Gemara's] mind that [Rabbi Elazar's statement] came to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Akiva. And if this Rabbi Elazar were an Amora, it would be well understood, for it was obvious to him that the halakhah does not follow Rabbi Akiva; however, he is Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, who is a Tanna, as is proven in [the chapter] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 75b). And it appears [to Tosafot] that it entered [the Gemara's] mind that according to no Tanna is [the offspring of] a yevamah to an outsider a mamzer, but rather specifically from [unions with] those subject to negative prohibitions of kin, as we learned in [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 49a and there): "Who is a mamzer? Any [offspring of a union with a] blood relative that is [prohibited] by a negative commandment." And [as for] that which we learned in [the chapter] HaIsha Rabbah (below, Yevamot 92a and there): "A woman whose husband and son went overseas, and [witnesses] said: 'Her husband died and afterward her son died,' and she married; and afterward they said to her: 'The matter was reversed' — she must leave (this one and that one), and the offspring is a mamzer (from this one and that one)," which implies that [the offspring of] a yevamah to an outsider is a mamzer — [the Gemara initially] thought that this is merely a [Rabbinic] penalty; even though it is taught in a baraita in the Gemara: "This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, who says that betrothal does not take effect with those subject to negative prohibitions" — that baraita had not been heard by [the questioner here].

Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:8:1.hebrew: ובספק אשת איש - לשון אחר שפי' בקונט' — דהיינו שכיב מרע שכתב גט לאשתו, ואע"ג דאין שם מחלוקת ב"ש וב"ה, הא נחלקו במגרש אשתו ולנה עמו בפונדקי — לא נהירא, דבהדיא חשיב הכא ההיא פלוגתא דהמגרש אשתו ולנה עמו בפונדקי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:8:1.english: "And with regard to an uncertain married woman" - Another explanation that was explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] — namely, that this refers to a person on his deathbed who wrote a bill of divorce for his wife, and although there is no dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel there, behold they disagreed with regard to one who divorces his wife and she lodges with him at an inn — does not appear correct, for [the Baraita] here explicitly lists that dispute of one who divorces his wife and she lodges with him at an inn.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:8:2.hebrew: בגט ישן - תימה: למ"ד בפ' [הזורק] בגיטין (ד' עט: ושם) דאם פטרה בגט ישן תנשא לכתחלה — למה היה להם למנוע? דמשמע דלא נמנעו משום דלא עשו כדבריהם, או משום דהוו מודעי להו ופרשי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14b:8:2.english: "With regard to an outdated bill of divorce" - [This is] puzzling: According to the one who says in the chapter [entitled] HaZorek in Gittin (79b and there) that if he divorced her with an outdated bill of divorce, she may marry ab initio — why should they have refrained [from marrying each other]? For [the Baraita] implies that they did not refrain [only] because they did not act in accordance with their [own] opinion, or because they would inform them and they would withdraw.
